```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

project_root <- normalizePath(
  if (file.exists("analysis/site/output/edna_first_linkage_audit.csv")) "." else file.path("..", ".."),
  winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
output_dir <- file.path(project_root, "analysis", "site", "output")
audit <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "edna_first_linkage_audit.csv"))
glmm <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "site_visit_glmm_performance.csv"))
effects <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "site_visit_brms_fixed_effects.csv"))
performance <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "site_visit_model_performance.csv"))
thresholds <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "site_visit_threshold_performance.csv"))
curve <- read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "site_visit_brms_percent_positive.csv"))
```

## Corrected observation unit

The previous operational models started from each cull dive and looked
backwards for an eligible eDNA event. The corrected analysis starts with an
eDNA sampling campaign and takes the first subsequent visit to every cull site.
All dives at that site and date are combined into one count and effort total.

Individual eDNA-event reversal would duplicate outcomes. The selected
campaign-to-site design retains 519 unique response visits with no duplication.

```{r}
kable(
  audit |>
    transmute(
      Design = design, Rows = n_rows, `eDNA events` = n_edna_events,
      `Site visits` = n_site_visits,
      `Duplicated outcomes` = duplicated_outcome_rows,
      `Median lag (days)` = round(median_lag_days, 1),
      `Median distance (m)` = round(median_distance_m)
    )
)
```

## Hierarchical model

    COTS count ~ % positive + distance + elapsed time
                 + offset(log(total bottom time))
                 + (1 | reef) + (1 | cull site) + (1 | eDNA campaign)

The fast GLMM screen strongly supports retaining all three grouping terms.

```{r}
kable(
  glmm |>
    transmute(
      Model = model, AIC = round(AIC, 1), `Delta AIC` = round(delta_AIC, 1),
      `Reef SD` = round(reef_sd, 2), `Site SD` = round(site_sd, 2),
      `Campaign SD` = round(campaign_sd, 2),
      `0.04 crossing (%)` = round(crossing_004, 1)
    )
)
```

The production BRMS model retained 8,000 post-warmup draws. All R-hat values
are 1.00 and it has no divergent transitions. Its 0.04 marginal crossing is
`r round(approx(curve$expected, curve$edna_pct, xout = 0.04)$y, 1)`% positive.

```{r}
kable(
  effects |>
    transmute(
      Term = term, Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
      `95% lower` = round(Q2.5, 3), `95% upper` = round(Q97.5, 3)
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-cap: "Site-visit BRMS grouping comparison, posterior effects, marginal percent-positive response, and distance-time context."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(project_root, "plots", "site_visit_brms_four_panel.png"))
```

## Boosted trees

The concentration-free Poisson boosted tree was tuned with complete eDNA
campaigns held out. Its partial-dependence intervals use 100 whole-reef
bootstrap samples.

```{r}
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-cap: "Site-visit boosted-tree validation, importance and whole-reef bootstrap partial dependence."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(project_root, "plots", "site_visit_brt_four_panel.png"))
```

## Ensemble validation

All model comparisons use the same five complete-campaign holdouts.

```{r}
kable(performance |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))))
```

The expected-CPUE ensemble uses 59% BRMS and 41% BRT. Threshold probabilities
favour BRMS more strongly: 81% at 0.02, 90% at 0.04 and 93% at 0.08.

```{r}
kable(
  thresholds |>
    transmute(
      Threshold = threshold, Model = model, AUC = round(AUC, 3),
      Brier = round(Brier, 3), Cutoff = round(cutoff, 2),
      F1 = round(F1, 3), Recall = round(recall, 3),
      Precision = round(precision, 3), Specificity = round(specificity, 3),
      `False negatives` = false_negatives
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-cap: "Complete-campaign held-out assessment of the corrected BRMS, BRT and ensemble."
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(project_root, "plots", "site_visit_ensemble_assessment.png"))
```

## Deployment

The versioned object is
analysis/site/output/reefDNA_site_visit_model_bundle.rds. It accepts percent
positive, distance, elapsed days, optional effort, reef, cull-site and campaign
identifiers through reefDNA::predict_reef_cpue().

The primary outputs are calibrated exceedance probabilities and expected CPUE
with uncertainty. Alert cutoffs maximize F1 on these out-of-fold predictions
and should remain provisional until the operational costs of false negatives
and false positives are specified.
